data.title: NHTSA Proposes Easing Manual Lighting Control Rules for Driverless Vehicles Like Cybercab
data.description:
The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has proposed changes to federal vehicle lighting regulations that could affect Tesla’s Cybercab, which is already facing a separate audit over its road-legal certification. 

The proposal would remove certain manual lighting control requirements for autonomous vehicles designed without steering wheels or pedals.

Under the current Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard (FMVSS) No. 108, vehicles must meet requirements for manually operated lighting controls. These include switches for turn signals, hazard warning lights, and headlight beam selection, even though fully driverless vehicles may have no human driver to operate them.

NHTSA’s proposed changes would limit those requirements to vehicles equipped with manual driving controls. Vehicles operating exclusively through an automated driving system (ADS) would therefore have greater flexibility in how their lighting systems are designed, without needing conventional switches intended for human drivers.

The agency explained that the proposed revisions are intended “to remove unnecessary requirements and to provide design flexibility without impact on vehicle safety.”

The changes could be significant for Tesla’s Cybercab, which was designed without a steering wheel or pedals. NHTSA opened an audit in September examining how Tesla self-certified the vehicle under existing federal safety standards, with the automaker subsequently receiving additional time to respond. 

Beyond removing certain manual control requirements, NHTSA is also proposing optional cyan-coloured exterior lights to identify vehicles operating without human supervision. The blue-green colour was selected partly because it is distinct from the blue lights used by law enforcement.

Manufacturers would not be required to install them, and Mercedes-Benz previously tested similar lights on public roads in California between 2023 and 2025.

The proposal also includes changes to headlight testing voltages and removes requirements governing vertical headlight arrangements. Tesla has not commented on the proposal.

The proposed regulations are scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on October 26, 2026, followed by a 30-day public comment period through regulations.gov.

data.title: New Tesla Roadster Goes on Public Display for the First Time at Petersen Museum
data.description:
The new Tesla Roadster, whose cold gas thrusters Lars Moravy says are built for production, will go on public display for the first time this weekend at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles.

The museum says the Roadster will sit in its main lobby from Saturday, October 24 through Tuesday, October 27, a limited four-day appearance.

According to the Petersen’s vehicle page, it is the same car that shared the stage with Elon Musk and the Tesla team at the unveiling in McGregor, Texas.

The museum describes it as the first chance for the public to see the vehicle up close. The Petersen is at 6060 Wilshire Blvd and is open daily from 10 AM to 6 PM.

Since the Roadster will be sitting in the lobby, a ticket is not needed to view the car this weekend.

For more on the car itself, here is what we’ve learned about the new Roadster since its reveal, and Musk’s claim that the Roadster will perform its stunts autonomously.

The Petersen previously added a Cybertruck to its “Inside Tesla” exhibit in 2023.

  • Lars Moravy says Tesla Roadster’s cold gas thrusters are built for production, not just show
  • What we’ve learned about the new Tesla Roadster since its reveal

data.title: Tesla Robotaxi expands Austin service to COTA, extends hours to 1 AM ahead of F1 weekend
data.description:
Tesla has stretched its Robotaxi service in Austin, Texas, to cover Circuit of the Americas (COTA) and run until 1 AM, less than a week after Cybercab rides were extended to midnight in the city.

The change was first shared on X by Sawyer Merritt, just as Austin gets ready to host the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at the track this weekend.

According to an updated to the Robotaxi mobile app, the updated service area map now includes the area around the racetrack.

Alongside the service area expansion, customers can now request a Robotaxi until 1 AM, an hour later than the previous midnight cut-off, which had only been in place since October 17.

Before that, Robotaxi rides in Austin ended at 11 PM, which is also when Cybercab service wrapped up each night when the two-seat vehicles first joined the fleet.

COTA sits southeast of downtown Austin, and several other X users also posted that the geofence now reaches the track ahead of race weekend.

The Austin update follows a busy week for the program, with Tesla publishing a Robotaxi safety report claiming zero injuries and confirming on its earnings call that the Cybercab is heading to Dallas next month.

Tesla’s Model Y Robotaxis already operate in Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando and Tampa, while the Cybercab is currently only available in Austin.

Related Articles:

  • Tesla Cybercab Extends Daily Operating Hours to Midnight in Austin
  • Tesla Cybercab heading to Dallas next month
  • Tesla Launches Robotaxi Safety Report, Claims Zero Injuries Over 3.1 Million Autonomous Miles

data.title: Tesla launches Supercharger for Business and Semi Charging for Business in Canada
data.description:
Tesla has brought Supercharger for Business to Canada, along with its Semi Charging for Business program, so Canadian companies can now buy Tesla chargers for their own sites.

Livio Caputo of Tesla’s Charging for Business team shared the Canadian launch on LinkedIn, as first reported by EVwire.

“The goal is to offer Charging for Business in every market where Tesla runs charging, 55+ countries and growing, with the same hardware, software and service we use ourselves,” Caputo wrote.

For passenger vehicles, Canadian hosts have to buy at least four Supercharger posts, according to Tesla’s Canadian Supercharger for Business page.

Tesla’s Canadian Supercharger for Business page also says the white-labelled stalls work with all EVs, can show up on the in-car map and come with a 97% uptime guarantee, while V4 posts are rated at up to 500 kW.

On the truck side, businesses need a minimum of two posts and can pick between the Megacharger and the Basecharger.

Tesla’s Semi Charging for Business page rates the Megacharger at up to 1.2 MW, which Tesla says can restore as much as 60% of a Semi’s range within half an hour.

The slower Basecharger, rated at 120 kW, targets depot and overnight charging and takes about four hours to restore that same 60%, with deliveries estimated to start in early 2027.

Owners can use their own installer with help from a Tesla Design Engineer, or have Tesla do the install, and then set pricing through Tesla’s portal while Tesla handles servicing.

Neither Canadian page lists pricing, and buyers are directed to a contact form instead.

In B.C., R.R. Plett Trucking is planning Canada’s first Tesla Megachargers in Langley and Kamloops.

The carrier expects to take delivery of 12 Tesla Semis in June 2027.

Related Articles:

  • Canada’s first Tesla Semi Megachargers to begin construction next month in B.C.

data.title: Porsche Delivers 38,730 EVs Through September as Electric Share Passes One in Five
data.description:
Over one in five of the Porsches handed to buyers worldwide so far this year has been fully electric. Porsche’s nine-month delivery report breaks out its three EVs, and adding them up gives 38,730 electric deliveries from January through September, or about 21.7% of the brand’s 178,532 total by our calculation.

That’s a notable shift for a company whose first EV, the Taycan, has spent the past while dealing with headlines like a battery fire class-action lawsuit.

The Macan Electric is doing most of the heavy lifting, accounting for well over half of Porsche EV deliveries on its own. The new Cayenne Electric has also made a quick start, even though it only arrived with customers in the summer.

The Taycan is heading the other way, with deliveries down 31% from a year earlier.

Porsche’s overall numbers meanwhile are under pressure. The brand delivered 178,532 vehicles over the nine months, down 16% from 212,509 a year earlier. Weakness in China, the end of 718 production and the wind-down of the combustion Macan, which ended production this summer, all weighed on results, and deliveries in China alone fell by a third.

With the gas-powered Macan gone, that nameplate will lean more heavily on the electric version from here on out. Of the 51,025 Macans delivered so far this year, 27,996 were combustion models. The Cayenne remains Porsche’s best-selling line overall, with 59,586 deliveries and only a 2% decline. The 911 was a bright spot, rising 12% to 42,217 units.

North America remains Porsche’s largest region, with 56,088 deliveries despite a 13% drop, which the automaker puts down to the end of the 718 and a strong run of Macan Electric sales in the prior year. Porsche hasn’t released a separate Canadian breakdown.

Elsewhere, deliveries in Europe outside Germany fell 11%, while Germany itself was down 7% and Porsche’s overseas and emerging markets slipped 19%.

data.title: SpaceX in Talks to Access 80,000 US Cell Towers for Starlink Mobile: Report
data.description:
SpaceX is in talks with major US tower companies to gain access to as many as 80,000 cell sites for Starlink Mobile, following the company’s FCC approval to acquire Tristar’s AWS-3 spectrum. The towers would give SpaceX a ground network to work alongside its direct-to-cell satellites.

Crown Castle is among the tower owners SpaceX is negotiating with, according to people familiar with the matter who spoke to Bloomberg. American Tower and Vertical Bridge, the other two large tower owners in the US, could also be involved. American Tower declined to comment, while SpaceX and Vertical Bridge did not respond to requests for comment. Any agreements could be worth billions of dollars.

Crown Castle CEO Chris Hillabrant did not name SpaceX during the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday, but he did not rule it out either. “You can assume that we’re talking to all parties,” said Hillabrant, who also called SpaceX’s recent purchase of low-band spectrum a “huge milestone.”

SpaceX’s goal is to become the fourth national wireless carrier in the US, and Elon Musk outlined the plan on SpaceX’s own earnings call. “We will be building out our terrestrial networks so there’s broad-based connectivity anywhere that SpaceX and Starlink are allowed to operate,” said Musk. He added that satellite launches and spectrum “will pave the way for Starlink Mobile to become a major mobile carrier in the US.”

The FCC has already approved SpaceX to operate 15,000 satellites that connect directly to phones, and Starlink Mobile now has more than 22 million monthly users.

T-Mobile already partners with SpaceX on direct-to-cell service in the US, and has expanded its Starlink satellite roaming to Canada and New Zealand.

Related Articles:

  • FCC Approves SpaceX Deal for Tristar’s AWS-3 Spectrum to Expand Starlink Direct-to-Device Service
  • Starlink Mobile Tops 22 Million Monthly Users as SpaceX Eyes Becoming a Major U.S. Carrier

data.title: Tesla building Western Canada’s first factory-owned Collision Centre in Port Coquitlam: Scoop
data.description:
Tesla owners in B.C. who end up in a fender bender may soon have a new place to get their cars fixed, straight from the automaker itself.

Tesla has announced it plans to build its own collision repair centre in Port Coquitlam, the same city where it opened a 60,000-square-foot Service and Delivery Center last year.

In a post on LinkedIn, Rishi Bakshi, Tesla’s new BC Collision Manager, said he is leading the launch of what he called “Western Canada’s very first factory-owned and operated Tesla Collision Center.”

According to Bakshi’s LinkedIn profile, he previously spent more than a decade at Boyd Autobody & Glass as its regional development and area manager for B.C., before working as a regional manager for Speedy Glass in B.C.

He added that the company is now putting together the facility’s founding team.

Who Tesla is hiring

According to Bakshi, Tesla is recruiting in Port Coquitlam for collision body technicians at every level from apprentice to journeyperson, along with paint preppers and detailers.

He pointed applicants to open listings on Tesla’s Career’s website and said new hires would get repair training directly from the manufacturer, including work on aluminum and structural components.

Listings include roles for a Collision Technician and an Apprentice Collision Technician.

Why it matters

A factory-run centre would let Tesla handle that work in-house, in a province with one of the highest EV adoption rates in North America.

Some B.C. body shops, such as AutoMind in Coquitlam, already belong to Tesla’s approved collision centre program, and get Tesla training and tooling but are independently owned. On its collision support page, Tesla describes its own collision centres as facilities that handle everything from cosmetic fixes to full structural repairs.

Port Coquitlam would be Tesla’s third factory-owned collision centre in Canada. The first, a dedicated Tesla Collision Center in Oakville, Ontario, opened in 2022, while a second opened in Montreal in 2023.

Tesla hasn’t announced when the new Collision Centre will open or where in Port Coquitlam it will be located.

data.title: Tesla Pulls the Plug on Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand
data.description:
Tesla has told Australians and New Zealanders holding Cybertruck reservations that the right-hand-drive version of its electric pickup won’t be coming after all.

The email landed in inboxes on Friday morning in both countries, with a number of customers sharing the email on social media.

“After careful consideration, plans to produce Cybertruck for Australia and New Zealand have been discontinued. As a result, we’re unable to fulfill your reservation and it will be cancelled,” Tesla wrote.

Customers were told a separate message with refund details would follow, and that any money they paid would be returned within 30 days. Because both countries drive on the left, the truck would have needed a dedicated right-hand-drive build, and that is the version Tesla has now decided not to make.

As an apology for “any inconvenience caused,” Tesla is offering affected customers 12 months of FSD (Supervised) at no charge, but it only applies to buyers who place an order for a Model 3 or Model Y. With the subscription running AU$149 (C$147) a month in that market, the offer works out to roughly AU$1,788 (C$1,759) for the year, but it does nothing for buyers who had their hearts set on the truck itself.

For many, the email closes out a wait that began when the Cybertruck was unveiled in 2019. Australians put down AU$150 (C$148) to hold a spot, and the warning signs had been there for a while, with Tesla quietly pulling its Australian reservation page back in 2022.

Canadian buyers are in a very different position. The left-hand-drive Cybertruck remains on Tesla’s Canadian site, with the Premium All-Wheel Drive starting at $139,990 and the Cyberbeast at $167,990, both inflated due to the current tariff situation with the U.S.

data.title: Chery considers building vehicles in Canada using idle plants or partners: Report
data.description:
Chery is now looking at building vehicles in Canada, only days after the Chinese automaker shifted its Canadian sales launch to early next year.

Speaking with Bloomberg at the company’s Wuhu, China headquarters, executive vice president Guibing Zhang said Chery is weighing a few options, including using idle capacity at plants that already exist or teaming up with partners.

“Even without the American market, Canada is a market that is worth having a factory for manufacturing,” said Zhang. “We are looking for the suitable opportunity and communicating on the possible formats.”

According to the report, Chery is looking at idle capacity and talking with Canadian investors interested in Chinese carmakers, although Zhang didn’t name any companies.

Zhang also said fellow Chery vice president Charlie Zhang has been talking often with Industry Minister Mélanie Joly, who sat down with Chery, BYD and Geely representatives while visiting China in June.

“If we can find some good ways to merge with partners, not only just from investments from Chery but from different parties, and if we can get the manufacturing going — I think that is something that the Canadian government would welcome,” said Zhang.

If it goes ahead, the report says Chery could become the first Chinese automaker with a manufacturing presence in Canada.

Idle plants have been a recurring topic this year, with BYD, Geely and Chery reportedly considering Ontario’s CAMI plant and Stellantis looking at importing China-built Jeep EVs while its Brampton plant sits idle.

Related Articles:

  • Chery shifts target to early next year for Canadian launch
  • BYD, Geely, and Chery reportedly considering Ontario’s CAMI plant for Canadian production
  • Stellantis considers importing China-built Jeep EVs to Canada as Brampton plant sits idle

data.title: 2027 Ford Mustang Mach-E gets standard extended range battery and new Trail package
data.description:
While Ford has decided to kill the F-150 Lightning, they aren’t quite giving up yet on the Mustang Mach-E. The electric SUV is getting more range as standard and a new package aimed at gravel roads and campsites.

The automaker detailed the 2027 Mustang Mach-E on Thursday, a few weeks after its EV sales sank 80% in the third quarter as the Mach-E and Lightning struggled.

Extended range battery for every trim

For the first time, the extended range battery comes standard across the whole lineup, and the smaller pack is gone.

Select and Premium models get 88 kWh of usable capacity, while the GT and Rally carry 91 kWh.

Ford credits a new, cheaper front motor that matches the old unit’s performance. In the U.S., the Select RWD now starts at US$39,995 before destination.

Ford says final EPA range estimates will come closer to availability.

The new Mach-E Trail

The Trail is a factory-built US$2,295 package that can only be added to the Select eAWD.

It raises the ride height by 10 mm up front and 15 mm at the rear compared with the Select and Premium, using specially tuned passive struts and springs.

It also borrows the Rally’s steering rack, 19-inch dark grey wheels and Michelin CrossClimate 2 tires, and adds 400W Pro Power Onboard, with plugs behind the centre console and in the cargo area.

“It’s built for all-season, off-pavement excursions,” said Nick Rallis, Ford’s lead Mach-E vehicle integration engineer, adding that the tires bring “a significant traction benefit in winter conditions as well.”

Visually, it stands apart with a Carbon Black front fascia section and a Trail logo on the centre armrest.

Trail buyers also get 100,000 extra Ford Rewards points beyond the 22,000 given with every Mach-E, which can go toward accessories such as a Thule clamp-on cross bar kit.

What about Canada?

U.S. orders opened on October 22, and the Trail is expected to start arriving in the first quarter of 2027.

Ford.ca already teases the Trail package, but it still lists 2026 trims and hasn’t published Canadian pricing for the 2027 lineup.
